# 1 Clement Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 12

**12:1** Because of her faith and hospitality Rahab the harlot was saved. [Josh 2; 6]

**12:2** For when the spies were sent out to Jericho by Joshua son of Nun, the king of the land learned that they had come to spy out his country, and sent men to apprehend them, so that they might be put to death.

**12:3** So the hospitable Rahab took them in and hid them under the stalks of flax on the roof.

**12:4** And when the king's messengers came and said, "The men that were spying out the land came to you — bring them forth, for the king so commands," she answered: "The two men whom you seek left me and went away," and she showed them another direction.

**12:5** And she said to the men: "I know of a surety that the Lord God is delivering this city to you, for fear and dread of you has fallen upon its inhabitants. When therefore it comes to pass that you take it, save me and my father's house."

**12:6** And they said to her: "It shall be even as you have spoken to us. Therefore, when you perceive that we are coming, gather all your household under your roof, and they shall be saved; but all who are found outside your house shall perish."

**12:7** And further they gave her a sign, that she should hang a piece of scarlet from her house — making manifest that through the blood of the Lord there should be redemption for all who believe and hope in God.

---

*EMET: The scarlet cord as a type of Christ's blood (v.7) is a standard early Christian typological reading. Rahab is one of only two women praised by name in the faith-gallery (with Lot's wife as a negative example).*
